scope: New external research only; existing Havenline reference audit is separate. No source is Havenline canon or runtime proof.

core_videos.title: Splitter belt compression: timing-gap example
core_videos.visual_review: full-duration frame sampling at 1 fps; not continuous real-time playback

observed_windows.observation: Small isolated belt arrangement with a feed entering from above, an inserter adding from a chest at lower left, and two splitters joining a rightward route. Items traverse the physical segments. White diagnostics move through the junctions.

core_videos.documented_not_measured: Developer article attributes the unwanted output spacing to item arrival timing at the splitter. No numerical throughput or item conservation was independently measured.
core_videos.havenline_application: Test a junction with intermittent input; preserve predictable item spacing and do not visually skip a physical transfer.

core_videos.title: Splitter belt compression: corrected arrangement
core_videos.visual_review: full-duration frame sampling at 1 fps plus native-resolution 18s detail; not continuous real-time playback

observed_windows.observation: Same small connection arrangement continues to pass items from the feed/inserter through both junctions onto the output route.

core_videos.documented_not_measured: Article explains extending the splitter input ramp as a short buffer to resolve timing gaps. The exact correction is documented; this review does not claim a frame-accurate independent proof.
core_videos.havenline_application: Give mergers and dispatch shutters a small bounded holding position rather than letting simultaneous arrivals overlap.

core_videos.title: Drop lane indication and flipping
core_videos.visual_review: full-duration frame sampling at 1 fps plus native-resolution 13s detail; not continuous real-time playback

observed_windows.observation: Four chest/inserter pairs have yellow output markers; belt placement previews appear beneath them and differ by validity.
Selecting and adjusting individual inserters changes yellow drop-marker placement relative to belt lanes.

core_videos.documented_not_measured: Article says arrows indicate which belt side receives items and flip placement preserves intent. No Havenline two-lane belt requirement is implied.
core_videos.havenline_application: Show a durable direction arrow and explicit destination socket, including after rotation and mirroring. Prefer one readable lane for the compact Havenline camp.

core_videos.title: Landing pad unloading bay demonstration
core_videos.visual_review: full-duration actual-source-frame sampling at 1 fps plus native-resolution 0s and 39s details; not continuous real-time playback

observed_windows.observation: Close view of receiving/cargo structures, many external transfer arms, parallel belts and rail corridors.
Camera pulls back across repeated unloading rows and connected belt routes, exposing the separation of bulk storage area and outgoing transport.
The end transition starts to overlay a close cargo/transfer view on the pulled-back scene.

core_videos.documented_not_measured: Article permits inserters to unload to trains, chests or belts and discusses connection/range limits. Not a proof of any camp recipe, fair dispatch policy or maximum rate.
core_videos.havenline_application: Treat the storage house as inventory plus visible receiving and dispatch adapters; use short outward belts rather than copying factory scale.

core_videos.title: Dorner Conveyor Transfers - In Line, 90 Degrees, Side-to-Side, Powered Transfers, Roller Transfers
core_videos.visual_review: NOT VIEWED: indexed official title/description and manufacturer page verified; public stream retrieval failed with HTTP403/unavailable format
core_videos.documented_not_measured: Official description identifies in-line, side-to-side and 90-degree transfer choices designed to prevent product loss.
core_videos.havenline_application: Give corners, height changes and machine handoffs actual transfer geometry; do not draw a belt ending against a wall or a gap larger than the item.

core_videos.title: Lift Gate Conveyors: Create safe walkthroughs and maximize usable space
core_videos.visual_review: NOT VIEWED: indexed official title/description and manufacturer page verified; official Wistia embed returned an error and no decoded video was available
core_videos.documented_not_measured: Manufacturer describes a lifting conveyor section, handles and counterbalance to provide walk-through access.
core_videos.havenline_application: Reserve both camp gate paths. When a belt must cross a walk route, show a deliberate bridge/tunnel or gated crossing with mutually exclusive foot and item traffic.

additional_videos.title: Accumulation System with Product Elevator
additional_videos.classification: first-party manufacturer video; finite buffer/dispatch analogy
additional_videos.visual_review: NOT VIEWED: official indexed description and embedding confirmed only
additional_videos.documented_not_measured: Description discusses temporary accumulation during downstream equipment stoppage, controlled loading to levels, and first-in-first-out reintroduction.
additional_videos.havenline_application: A finite storage buffer absorbs a temporary stall; it is not a sink that erases goods. The precise stack counts and industrial rates do not belong in Havenline.

additional_videos.title: My Perfect Hotel
additional_videos.classification: official casual-game promotional trailer; candidate service-flow comparison
additional_videos.visual_review: NOT VIEWED: official indexed metadata/description only
additional_videos.documented_not_measured: Description establishes hotel management and service progression; it does not prove conveyor or cash routing.
additional_videos.havenline_application: Candidate only. Do not cite as observed evidence for a customer-counter layout; the user’s actual camp/reference footage should support that.

additional_videos.title: Machine rotation exposes a fluid-connection mismatch
additional_videos.classification: official developer negative-case demonstration; fluid/port-validation analogy
additional_videos.visual_review: full-duration frame sampling at 2 fps; not continuous real-time playback

observed_windows.observation: Machine selection/rotation changes the resource-marked connector orientations next to an existing pipe run.
A second pipe run is built from another port and fluid icons appear along it.

additional_videos.documented_not_measured: The surrounding article identifies this as an unwanted fluid-filter/pass-through condition and discusses a fix. This is a defect example, not desired material mixing.
additional_videos.havenline_application: After rotation or upgrade, revalidate port type/direction; incompatible goods should remain buffered and produce an understandable alert.

supporting_documents.title: Friday Facts #225 - Bots versus belts (part 2)
supporting_documents.evidence: Developer defines input priority, output priority and output filtering as different controls.
supporting_documents.application: Do not conflate splitting, priority and material filters in one unexplained junction.

supporting_documents.title: Belt transport system
supporting_documents.evidence: Documentation describes split/merge behavior, blocked outputs, priorities, filtered outputs and throughput bottlenecks.
supporting_documents.application: Blocked filtered items should not silently become an unrelated resource or escape through a wrong destination.

supporting_documents.title: Conveyor Splitter
supporting_documents.evidence: Indexed source describes routing among unblocked outputs and eventually stopping input after all outputs and internal buffer fill. Direct page open returned403; no visual evidence.
supporting_documents.application: Full destination -> finite output/transfer buffers -> upstream wait. Do not assume its game-specific nine-item buffer for Havenline.

supporting_documents.title: Friday Facts #405 - Whole belt reader, New logistics GUI
supporting_documents.evidence: Developer explains reducing clutter while showing contents over a connected transport line.
supporting_documents.application: Use an optional flow-inspection overlay with destination and blocked reason; avoid permanent diagnostic clutter.

archive_policy: Do not publish local-media, downloaded full HTML, or failed media responses. Commit register, original analysis and narrowly selected attributed evidence stills only as appropriate. No source-media licence was established.
